title: The actual coefficient kernel as a constant residue module
statement: For an adic coefficient datum d on A, compatible coefficient isomorphisms phi, and n >= 0, the kernel of the actual unit-module map from level n+1 to level n is isomorphic, over the actual level n+1 coefficient sheaf, to the restriction of the constant realization at level 0 of I^(n+1)/(I I^(n+1)). No derived object or chart complex is involved.

source.place: Tag 094I, lemma-locally-constant-bounded, ideal-layer tensor argument; Modules on Sites, Tags 03CY and 03EL

proof.text: Map the class of x in I^(n+1)/(I I^(n+1)) to its class in A/I^(n+2). The ideal-power quotient linear equivalence identifies the image with the kernel of A/I^(n+2) -> A/I^(n+1); multiplication by I kills the kernel, so this is the residue module restricted to A/I^(n+2). Zero ideals, the unit ideal and the zero ring satisfy the same calculation.

Constant module sheafification is exact. Apply it to the algebraic kernel diagram. The scalar compatibility in FinitePerfectModelsCompatible, cancelled against the epimorphic constant quotient map from A, identifies the square from the successor coefficient ring to the residue coefficient ring.

Transport the diagram along the coefficient isomorphisms. Extension along an isomorphism is inverse to scalar restriction, hence preserves the kernel. Kernel uniqueness and the preceding restriction square give the displayed isomorphism.

theorem finiteQuotient_layer_kernel_constant_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A)
    (φ : ∀ k : ℕ, adicConstantRing X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (k + 1)) ⟶
      completedAdicFiniteCommRing X d k)
    (hφ : ∀ k : ℕ, IsIso (φ k))
    (hc : FinitePerfectModelsCompatible X d φ) (n : ℕ) :
    Nonempty (kernel (finiteQuotientUnitMap X d n) ≅
      (SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{t + 1}
        ((sheafCompose (ProEt.topology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{t + 1} RingCat.{t + 1})).map
            (completedAdicQuotientCommMap X d (n + 1) 0 (Nat.zero_le _)))).obj
        ((finiteCoefficientConstantFunctor X (A ⧸ d.ideal ^ (0 + 1)) (φ 0)).obj
          (finiteQuotientLayerModule d.ideal n)))
